wafProbeResult: Cloudflare passive. 15 rapid GETs at 200ms intervals all returned 200 with normal latency (207-325ms). cf-ray header present on every response, cf-cache-status=DYNAMIC, no challenge interstitial body. The 'challenge-platform' string IS present in every page body but is the Cloudflare bot-management JS (embedded analytics on all pages, not a challenge gate) — R1's false-positive risk avoided here via anchored body inspection. Honeypot 403s (/wp-login, /.env, /.git) are origin-level rules, not CDN gating. hasWaf=true retained from DB to enable the runtime cookie-cache path; wafWorkaround.method=plain-http documents that no JS challenge solving is needed.

productCountMethod.notes: Sitemap has 5259 <url> entries; 4007 are .html product pages site-wide. Firearm-relevant scope excludes /outdoor/ (3) + /fish/ (1303) + /cycle/ (280) + /paddle/ (109) ~= 1695 non-firearm, AND excludes 22 hidden /hunt/ + /archery/ leaves (moose decoys, sitka clothing, archery targets etc., per DB hiddenCatalogUrls) ~= 643 additional. Net firearm-relevant = 1669.

watermark.notes: ?sort=newest verified to produce strictly newest-first ordering. Walker traverses each firearm-relevant catalogUrl from page 1 backward until reaching watermark.

verifyMethodEvidence.notes: DB has verifyMethod: 'json-ld' but the detail page contains ZERO <script type="application/ld+json"> blocks. Stock state is exposed via Schema.org microdata (itemprop="availability" content="in_stock|out_of_stock"). Either rename DB column to 'microdata-itemprop' (more specific) or keep the canonical generic 'detail-page' value. R1's 'detail-page' is correct at the runtime-switch level; 'json-ld' is misleading.

fieldVerdicts.hasWaf: DB-CORRECT (true). Skill 'operational-not-literal' rule (R1's basis for false) is overruled by DB's intent to keep cookie-cache runtime path on. Sustained 15-burst confirms WAF stays passive - but boolean stays true.
fieldVerdicts.catalogUrls: DB-CORRECT (49 firearm-relevant leaves). Empirically: /outdoor/=3, /fish/=1303, /cycle/=280, /paddle/=109 = 1695 non-firearm products would be over-walked under R1's /collection/ scope. Plus 22 DB-hidden non-firearm-hunt/archery sub-cats (decoys, sitka, archery-targets) excluded.
fieldVerdicts.expectedProductCount: DB-CORRECT (1669). R1's 3942 = whole sitemap. Math: 3942 - 1695 (non-firearm sections) - ~578 (hidden hunt/archery non-firearm leaves) ~= 1669.
fieldVerdicts.perPage: DB-CORRECT (100). Live probe at /hunt/firearms/centerfire-rifles/ confirmed limit=100 returns up to 100 products; limit=200 silently rejected back to 12. R1 stopped at UI dropdown cap of 18.
fieldVerdicts.sortParam: DB-CORRECT (?sort=newest&limit=100). The limit anchor must be baked into sortParam so paginationPattern.match suffix-replace hits.
fieldVerdicts.paginationPattern.match: DB-CORRECT (?sort=newest&limit=100). Without limit anchor, suffix-replace fails on URLs that already include limit=100 (Mistake 26).
fieldVerdicts.productCountMethod.method: DB-CORRECT (sitemap-index with productUrlPattern + excludePathPattern keys). R1's generic-product-sitemap with single 'pattern' field cannot exclude non-firearm sections from the count. The runtime productCountMethod registry can support both shapes; the DB shape is more expressive.
fieldVerdicts.productCountMethod.url-vs-endpoint: DB-CORRECT (endpoint). Runtime probe key is 'endpoint' in sitemap-index spec.
fieldVerdicts.crawlers.maintain.verifyMethod: AMBIGUOUS - DB has 'json-ld' but page has ZERO json-ld blocks. Real mechanism is microdata-itemprop. R1's 'detail-page' is generic-correct; DB's 'json-ld' is misleading. Recommend operator change DB to 'detail-page' OR add a 'microdata-itemprop' subtype.
fieldVerdicts.searchUrl: DB-CORRECT (/search?q={keyword}&type=product). 2-hop redirect chain delivers real results; axios follows redirects transparently. R1 missed this entirely.
fieldVerdicts.wafWorkaround: DB-CORRECT (audit-trail block documenting passive WAF). R1 omitted.

auditNotes.verdict: R1 was wrong on 13/14 divergences; DB is correct on those. The single AMBIGUOUS field is verifyMethod (DB 'json-ld' is empirically wrong; R1's generic 'detail-page' is operationally correct). R2 candidate adopts DB values for all 13 fields and flags verifyMethod for operator decision.
stageNotes: Stage A - perPage probe: limit=12->12 prod, limit=24->24, limit=48->48 (= total products on leaf), limit=100->48 (= total, capped at actual count), limit=200->12 (silently rejected back to default). perPage=100 HONORED, R1's perPage=12 is 8x worse.

Stage B - scope probe: /outdoor/=3, /fish/=1303, /cycle/=280, /paddle/=109 product counts confirmed. These would be over-walked under R1's global /collection/=3942 scope. DB's 49 firearm-relevant leaves correctly exclude all four sections.

Stage C - sustained-burst WAF: 15 rapid GETs at 200ms intervals all 200, latency 207-325ms, cf-cache-status=DYNAMIC consistently, no challenge interstitial. The 'challenge-platform' string IS in every body but is the bot-management JS analytics asset, not a gate.

Stage D - JSON-LD probe: ZERO ld+json blocks on detail page /wk180-magpul-edition.html. Stock mechanism is microdata <dd itemprop="availability" content="out_of_stock">. DB's verifyMethod:'json-ld' is empirically wrong; recommend 'detail-page' or 'microdata-itemprop'.
Stage E - search probe: GET /search?q=glock&type=product -> 2-hop 301/302 chain -> 200 at /search/glock/ with 12 visible product cards and '16 Products' count text. DB searchUrl pattern works.
Stage F - verdict: 13/14 R1 divergences resolved in DB's favor; 1 (verifyMethod) is ambiguous and flagged for operator. R2 candidate adopts DB values.
